To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a detailed heat and mas transfer model for solar thermochemical reactors that was used to design a 5 kWth reactor to produce 1158 K outlet temperature with stoichiometric deviation of 0.07 and storage efficiency of 62% while avoiding overheating and promoting particle residence times.
a solar thermochemical reactor was designed, modeled and optimized, and the flow properties of aluminum doped calcum magnanite particles were characterized and incorporated into the model.

a two step thermochemical cycle based on the reduction and oxidation of aluminum doped CaMnO3 particles was developed and demonstrated for solar energy storage in a 5 kWth reactor operating under vacuum.

a solar thermal reactor design and particle characterization for solar thermochemical storage based on aluminum doped calcium manganese oxide.
the development of a two-step solar thermochemical cycle for energy storage and delivery.
the design and optimization of a solar thermochemical reactor that operates in a continuous mode to thermally reduce particles of aluminum doped calcuim manganite.
